full_text:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday hit out at the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the law and order situation in Punjab, citing the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and the death of a father in Dirba who allegedly consumed poison under pressure.
Shah said the two incidents had raised serious questions about the safety of people in Punjab, and announced that the Union Home Ministry would seek the state government’s response on both cases.
“Punjab is grappling today with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism, and organized crime. The biggest question before the Bhagwant Mann government is: ultimately, who will bear the responsibility for the safety of Punjab’s people?” Shah posted on X.
‘Grave allegations’ by Jhota’s father
Referring to Jhota, who was shot dead in Mansa on October 13 while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs, Shah said the activist’s father had made serious allegations against the AAP government and its MLA.
“In Dirba, a father succumbing to pressure and consuming poison, and in Mansa, the broad-daylight murder of Parvinder Singh Jhotta—who had raised his voice against drugs—have raised serious questions about Punjab’s law and order situation. Parvinder’s father has leveled grave allegations against the ‘AAP’ government and their MLA. The Home Ministry will also seek responses from the Punjab government on both these incidents,” he wrote.
“In Punjab, the drug trade is growing day by day, the threat of organized crime is increasing, and questions are being raised about the protection of those who speak out against drugs,” Shah added.
‘People want answers, not promises’
Targeting Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann directly, Shah said, “Bhagwant Mann ji, the people of Punjab do not want promises—they want answers; not announcements, but results; decisive strikes against drug networks; and an impartial investigation into any political patronage received by criminals.”
